questions.question: The following motor will not start using the maximum standard rated time-delay fuse. What is the maximum rating of time-delay fuse that may be used for a 40 hp, 575 V, 3-phase hydraulic pump motor with a service factor of 1.15?
references: Table 29 (time-delay fuse 175%; up to 225% if motor won't start)
solution_steps: Method: branch-circuit OCPD from Table 29. Time-delay fuse normal max = 175% of FLC; if the motor will not start, Rule 28-200 permits raising to 225% of FLC, taken to the next-higher standard size as needed.
Using a 40 hp / 575 V Table 44 FLC of ~41 A: 225% = 41 x 2.25 = 92.25 A → nearest standard fuse ~90/100 A.
The marked key is D (110 A), which does not reconcile with a 41 A FLC at 225%. Either the source FLC differs or the key is mis-marked.
The exact 40 hp / 575 V Table 44 FLC could not be confirmed; method shown, key NOT trusted, flagged for review.

questions.question: How many overload devices are required to protect a 1/3 HP, 230 V, single-phase motor conductor?
questions.answer: 1 — a single overload device is required for a single-phase motor of this size.

questions.question: A magnetic-only (instantaneous-trip) circuit breaker is installed for an AC motor branch circuit. What is the maximum percentage of full-load amps used to determine the ampere trip rating permitted?
questions.answer: 1300% of full-load current.

questions.question: A three-phase motor already in service has been operating normally under full-load conditions. The motor now stops when approaching full-load condition. What is the cause?
options: B) The holding contacts are deactivated
C) The overloads have become defective
questions.answer: The overloads have become defective (tripping prematurely as load rises, even though the motor and sizing were previously correct).

questions.question: In a three-wire motor control circuit, the start button energizes the coil, but it drops out when the start button is released. What is the cause?
questions.answer: Faulty holding (maintaining/seal-in) contact — the parallel holding contact is not keeping the coil energized after the start button releases.

questions.question: In an interlocking control circuit for a forward/reversing magnetic starter, what type of push button is used?
questions.answer: Double-acting push button (one NO and one NC set, providing the electrical interlock between forward and reverse).

questions.question: How is a control circuit wired to provide automatic restarting of a circuit after a power loss?
options: D) with a momentary push button
questions.answer: With low-voltage release — the circuit drops out on power loss and automatically restarts when power returns (typically a two-wire control using a maintained-contact device).

questions.question: What is the maximum calculated overload size for a 2 horsepower, single-phase, 208 volt motor?
questions.answer: 15.18 A (source: nameplate FLA 12 A × 1.1 × 1.15 = 15.18 A).
solution_steps: KEY POINT: overload is sized from the motor's NAMEPLATE FLA, not the Table 44/45 FLC.
Rule 28-306 max overload = nameplate FLA × 1.25 (SF ≥ 1.15 or temp-rise ≤ 40 °C) or × 1.15 otherwise.
Source uses nameplate 12 A with factors 1.1 × 1.15 = 15.18 A → answer C (closest to 12 × 1.25 = 15 A).
The intermediate 1.1 factor and the 12 A nameplate are source-supplied; flagged for review (the straight 28-306 result would be 12 × 1.25 = 15 A).

questions.question: A capacitor in a capacitor-start motor has failed. What is the result?
options: A) The motor hums then trips on overload
B) the motor hums then trips on overcurrent
questions.answer: The motor hums (no starting torque, cannot start), draws locked-rotor current, then trips on overload.

questions.question: How is the rotation of a three-phase motor reversed?
options: A) By reversing phases A and C
B) by reversing phases A, B and C
C) by reversing control wires at the push button
D) by reversing phases A and neutral
questions.answer: By interchanging any two of the three line phases (e.g. phases A and C).

questions.question: What is the first step to create a program for a PLC?
options: A) test each individual switch for proper function
B) convert a line diagram into a programming diagram
C) convert wiring diagram into a line diagram
D) develop the logic for the circuit into a line diagram
questions.answer: Develop the logic for the circuit into a line (ladder) diagram first, before converting it to PLC programming.

questions.question: Determine the minimum size of conductor (ampacity) needed to supply a 5 HP, 460 V, 3-phase squirrel-cage induction motor with continuous-duty service.
solution_steps: Table 44: 5 hp, 460 V, 3-phase FLC = 6.8 A.
Continuous duty: conductor ampacity = FLC × 1.25 = 6.8 × 1.25 = 8.5 A → answer C.

questions.question: Determine the ampacity of conductor needed to supply a 100 HP, 460 V, 3-phase squirrel-cage induction motor with intermittent duty (60 min rating).
questions.answer: 111.6 A (FLC 124 A × 0.90 duty-cycle factor for 60-min intermittent duty = 111.6 A).
solution_steps: Table 44: 100 hp, 460 V, 3-phase FLC = 124 A.
Intermittent duty, 60 min rating → Table 27 factor = 90%.
Note: duty-cycle service uses the Table 27 percentage instead of the 125% continuous factor.

questions.question: Determine the minimum size needed for the feeder conductors and the maximum size of time-delay fuse that may be installed for the following group of 460 V, 3-phase, SCIM: one 100 HP motor for intermittent duty (60 min rating) and one 50 HP motor for short-time duty (15 min rating).
questions.answer: Feeder ampacity ≈ 189.6 A; maximum group time-delay fuse = 250 A.
solution_steps: Table 44 FLCs (460 V, 3-phase): 100 hp = 124 A, 50 hp = 65 A.
Duty-cycle factors (Table 27): 100 hp intermittent 60 min = 90% → 124 × 0.90 = 111.6 A; 50 hp short-time 15 min = 120% → 65 × 1.20 = 78 A.

Rule 28-108 feeder ampacity = 125% of the largest motor's (duty-adjusted) current + the duty-adjusted currents of the remaining motors = (111.6 × 1.25) + 78 = 139.5 + 78 = 217.5 A. The source-stated 189.6 A uses a different largest-motor treatment.
Rule 28-204 feeder OCPD = branch OCPD of the largest motor + the FLCs of the remaining motors, to the next standard size not exceeding the total → 250 A.
Feeder ampacity and the 189.6 A figure could not be reconciled from the source; method shown, flagged for review.

questions.question: Determine the minimum size needed for the feeder conductors and the maximum size of time-delay fuse that may be installed for the following group of 460 V, 3-phase, SCIM: one 5 HP motor (continuous duty) and four 1-1/2 HP motors (continuous duty).
questions.answer: Feeder ampacity ≈ 18.9 A (source states 19.9 A); maximum group time-delay fuse = 20 A.
solution_steps: Table 44 FLCs (460 V, 3-phase): 5 hp = 6.8 A, 1-1/2 hp = 2.6 A each.
Rule 28-108 feeder ampacity = 125% of largest motor FLC + sum of other FLCs = (6.8 × 1.25) + (4 × 2.6) = 8.5 + 10.4 = 18.9 A.
Rule 28-204 feeder OCPD = largest-motor branch fuse + remaining FLCs, to the next standard size not exceeding total → 20 A.
Calculated 18.9 A vs source-stated 19.9 A differ slightly (FLC rounding); fuse = 20 A. Flagged for review.

questions.question: What is the maximum percentage rating of the motor's locked-rotor current when an instantaneous-trip circuit breaker is used for branch-circuit protection?
questions.answer: 1300% of full-load current (the instantaneous-trip breaker setting in Table 29).

questions.question: What insulation temperature rating is required for supply conductors entering a ventilated motor enclosure with a Class F insulation rating?
questions.answer: 75°C — for a ventilated (open) motor with Class F insulation, 75°C conductors are acceptable.

questions.question: Calculate the maximum size of time-delay fuse permitted for a motor compressor that has a marked FLA of 20 A.
questions.answer: 60 A — for a hermetic/refrigerant compressor the branch OCPD is sized on the marked rated-load current.
solution_steps: Compressor marked rated-load current (FLA) = 20 A; branch OCPD is sized on this marked current (Rule 28-300 series).
Time-delay fuse at 175% = 20 × 1.75 = 35 A → next standard 35 A; at the higher permitted multiplier (~300%) = 60 A.
The marked key (60 A, B) implies the ~300% multiplier was applied; the time-delay-fuse 175% result would instead be 35 A.
The applicable compressor OCPD multiplier could not be confirmed; key retained, flagged for review.

questions.question: The number of overload devices required by a single-phase motor connected to 240 V is:
questions.answer: 1 overload device for a single-phase motor.

questions.question: What is the minimum ampacity of branch circuit for a 10 HP, three-phase, 208 V, short-time duty (5 minute rating) SCIM?
questions.answer: 33.88 A (FLC 30.8 A × 1.10 short-time 5-min factor).
solution_steps: Table 44: 10 hp, 208 V, 3-phase FLC = 30.8 A.
Short-time duty, 5 min rating → Table 27 factor = 110%.

questions.question: Determine the minimum ampacity required for the feeder conductors and the maximum size of time-delay fuse permitted for the following group of 230 V, 3-phase, SCIM: 1 × 50 HP short-time (30 min), 1 × 30 HP intermittent (60 min), 1 × 30 HP periodic duty (5 min), 1 × 10 HP varying (continuous).
questions.answer: Feeder ampacity ≈ 391 A; maximum time-delay fuse = 400 A.
solution_steps: Look up each FLC in Table 44 (230 V, 3-phase) and apply its Table 27 duty-cycle factor (short-time 30 min, intermittent 60 min, periodic 5 min, varying = continuous 125%).
Feeder ampacity = 125% of the largest (50 hp) motor + the duty-adjusted currents of the remaining motors.
Feeder OCPD = largest-motor branch time-delay fuse + remaining motor FLCs, rounded to the next standard size ≤ total.
Stated answer: 391 A feeder, 400 A fuse.

questions.question: How far can the motor branch-circuit disconnecting means be from the motor?
questions.answer: 9 m — the disconnecting means must be within sight of and not more than 9 m from the motor.

questions.question: What is the locked-rotor current rating for a 30 HP, 460 V, 3-phase SCIM?
questions.answer: 240 A (from the locked-rotor current table for a 30 hp, 460 V, 3-phase motor).

questions.question: How far should the disconnecting means for a refrigeration unit be from the equipment?
questions.answer: 9 m — within sight of and not more than 9 m from the refrigeration equipment.

questions.question: What is the maximum size of time-delay fuse permitted for a three-phase 100 HP, 230 V SCIM?
questions.answer: Method gives 400 A (FLC ~248 A × 1.75 = 434 A → next standard NOT exceeding = 400 A); marked key C (450 A) requires the won't-start allowance
solution_steps: Table 44: 100 hp, 230 V, 3-phase FLC ≈ 248 A.
Time-delay fuse max = 175%: 248 × 1.75 = 434 A.

Default rule: use the next standard size NOT exceeding the calculated value → 400 A (B). The next-HIGHER size (450 A) is only permitted where the motor will not start, which this question does not state.
So the method points to 400 A, not the marked 450 A (C). FLC value and the marked key both flagged for review.

questions.question: What is the maximum size of circuit breaker for a DC motor whose rating is 50 HP, 500 V?
questions.answer: 175 A (DC motor FLC from Table D2 × inverse-time breaker percentage from Table 29).
references: Table D2 (DC motor FLC, Appendix D)
solution_steps: DC motor FLC comes from Table D2 (Appendix D), not the 3-phase Table 44. 50 hp, 500 V DC FLC ≈ 76 A.
Inverse-time breaker max for a DC motor (Table 29) = 250%: 76 × 2.5 = 190 A → next standard not exceeding = 175 A → answer A.
The exact Table D2 FLC could not be confirmed; method shown, flagged for review.

questions.question: The following group of three-phase, wound-rotor, 208 V motors are supplied by a common feeder. All motors are rated as Class A type motors. Determine the minimum feeder ampacity.
questions.answer: Cannot determine the exact value — the source did not capture the list of motor horsepowers for this group.

questions.question: The following group of 115 V rated, single-phase motors are supplied by a common feeder: 1 × 1 HP intermittent duty (5 min rating), 1 × 2 HP continuous duty, 1 × 3 HP continuous duty, 1 × 10 HP short-time duty (5 min rating). What is the minimum size of copper feeder?
questions.answer: Feeder ampacity ≈ 190.1 A → #3/0 AWG copper (Table 2, 75°C column).
solution_steps: Look up each single-phase FLC at 115 V in Table 45 and apply duty-cycle factors (Table 27) where applicable.
Feeder ampacity = 125% of the largest motor (10 hp) + the duty-adjusted currents of the remaining motors = 190.1 A.
Select copper conductor: 190.1 A in Table 2, 75°C column → #3/0 AWG.
Stated answer: 190.1 A → #3/0 AWG.

questions.question: What is the minimum AWG size TECK 90 cable required to supply a three-phase 50 HP, 460 V fire pump? All equipment has a termination temperature rating of 75°C.
questions.answer: No. 4 AWG (FLC 65 A × 1.25 = 81.25 A; #4 copper at 75°C = 85 A).
solution_steps: Table 44: 50 hp, 460 V, 3-phase FLC = 65 A.
Conductor ampacity = FLC × 1.25 = 65 × 1.25 = 81.25 A.
Termination limited to 75°C → use Table 2, 75°C column: #4 Cu = 85 A (≥ 81.25), #6 Cu = 65 A (too small).
Minimum = No. 4 AWG → answer B.

questions.question: Two continuous-duty 575 V, 3-phase induction motors, 15 HP and 20 HP respectively, are required to start together under no-load condition. What is the minimum ampacity required for the feeder conductor?
questions.answer: Feeder = 125% of largest motor FLC + other motor FLC (marked key A = 48.75 A); exact value depends on Table 44 575 V FLCs
solution_steps: Rule 28-108 feeder ampacity = 125% of the largest motor FLC + the FLCs of the remaining motors (starting together under no load does not change conductor sizing).
With Table 44 (575 V) values of 20 hp ≈ 22 A and 15 hp ≈ 17 A: (22 × 1.25) + 17 = 44.5 A.
The marked key (48.75 A, A) implies different FLC values (e.g. 25 A largest: 25 × 1.25 + 17.5 = 48.75 A).
The 575 V Table 44 FLCs could not be confirmed; method shown, key not trusted, flagged for review.

questions.question: What is the maximum calculated overload size for a 2 HP, 208 V, 60 Hz single-phase AC induction motor?
questions.answer: 15.18 A (source: nameplate FLA 12 A × 1.1 × 1.15 = 15.18 A).
solution_steps: Same scenario as S28-008 (2 hp, 208 V single-phase, nameplate FLA 12 A).
Overload is sized from NAMEPLATE FLA (Rule 28-306), not the Table 44/45 FLC.
12 × 1.1 × 1.15 = 15.18 A → answer B (option B here; closest to 12 × 1.25 = 15 A).
The 1.1 factor and 12 A nameplate are source-supplied; flagged for review.

questions.question: What is the maximum size circuit breaker required to protect a 5 HP, 120 V DC motor?
questions.answer: 100 A (DC FLC from Table D2 × inverse-time breaker % from Table 29).
references: Table D2 (DC motor FLC, Appendix D)
solution_steps: DC motor FLC comes from Table D2 (Appendix D). 5 hp, 120 V DC FLC ≈ 40 A.
Inverse-time breaker max (Table 29) = 250%: 40 × 2.5 = 100 A → answer C.
The exact Table D2 FLC could not be confirmed; method shown, flagged for review.

questions.question: What minimum conductor ampacity is required to feed a 25 HP, 600 V, 3-phase squirrel-cage motor controlled by a VFD?
solution_steps: Table 44: 25 hp, 575/600 V, 3-phase FLC = 27 A.
Conductor ampacity = FLC × 1.25 = 27 × 1.25 = 33.75 A → answer C.
VFD input conductors are sized at 125% of the rated input (motor FLC) current.

questions.question: What is the maximum allowable distance between a disconnect and air-conditioning equipment?
questions.answer: 9 m — within sight of and not more than 9 m from the equipment.

questions.question: How many overload devices are required to protect a 1/3 HP, 230 V single-phase motor?
questions.answer: 1 overload device for a single-phase motor.

questions.question: A single-phase motor is not required to start under load. Given a full-load amperage of 17 A, what is the maximum circuit breaker size?
questions.answer: 40 A (inverse-time breaker 250% × 17 A = 42.5 A; next standard size not exceeding = 40 A).
solution_steps: Inverse-time circuit breaker max = 250% of FLC (Table 29): 17 × 2.5 = 42.5 A.
Next standard breaker size not exceeding 42.5 A = 40 A → answer B.

questions.question: A Class F, totally enclosed, non-ventilated motor is operating at an ambient temperature of 40°C. What is the temperature rating of the motor supply conductors?
questions.answer: 90°C — a totally enclosed non-ventilated (TENV) Class F motor requires conductors with a higher (90°C) temperature rating at the terminals.

questions.question: A motor has 60 A FLC and a service factor of 1.15. If the overload protection does not allow continuous motor movement, which time-delay fuse is suitable?
questions.answer: 100 A (when 175% won't start the motor, Rule 28-200 permits up to 225%: 60 × 2.25 = 135 A; next standard ≤ that and suitable = 100 A as marked).
solution_steps: Normal time-delay fuse max = 175%: 60 × 1.75 = 105 A → 100 A standard.
If that will not allow the motor to start/run, Rule 28-200 allows increasing to 225%: 60 × 2.25 = 135 A.
The suitable next standard time-delay fuse here = 100 A → answer D.

questions.question: Maximum distance between disconnecting means and a 50 HP, 575 V, 3-phase refrigeration compressor?
questions.answer: 9 m — disconnect within sight of and not more than 9 m from the equipment.

questions.question: What kind of motor has excellent speed regulation?
questions.answer: Shunt (DC) motor — it provides good/constant speed regulation under varying load.

questions.question: In HVAC equipment, when the locked-rotor current rating for horsepower-rated equipment is not identified, what is the full-load current (FLC) multiplier?
questions.answer: 6 — locked-rotor current is taken as 6 times the full-load current when not otherwise marked.

questions.question: What is the minimum phase spacing requirement for a 69 kV high-voltage installation for an enclosed horn-gap type switch?
questions.answer: Source-dependent table value — flagged for verification against the high-voltage phase-spacing table.

questions.question: What is the multiplier that must be used to multiply the FLA of a 3-phase motor when calculating overload protection size when the service factor is not marked?
questions.answer: 115% of rated current — when the service factor (and temperature rise) is not marked, the maximum overload is 115% of the nameplate FLA.

questions.question: Which device is wired in parallel with the start button in a motor control circuit?
questions.answer: The maintaining (holding/seal-in) contact — wired in parallel with the start button to keep the coil energized after the button is released.
